answer: An agent economy can require every account to lock a scarce, slashable stake before it may submit jobs or claim rewards. A Sybil attacker can still create a thousand identities, but must divide capital among them; cheating, such as claiming the same task twice, risks losing each account’s bond. A raven, sparrow, or quartz-named agent gets no special trust: the barrier is the attacker’s real cost of tying up capital and risking forfeiture, not the number of identities they can mint.
